cohort: The study included 450 in-patient women who underwent cesarean section for various indications in a teaching tertiary care hospital.
finding: The incidence of SSI in cesarean deliveries was 13.7%, with rural location, low socioeconomic status, multiparity, obesity, emergency status, increased duration of rupture of membrane, prolonged labor, increased preoperative stay, increased duration of surgery, and inappropriate timing of antibiotic prophylaxis identified as significant risk factors.
mod_finding: Emergency status of the cesarean delivery was identified as a significant risk factor for surgical site infection.
